title: Asking for Help at Work — Polite Questions and Clarification
description: Learn to ask for help, repeat instructions, and clarify what you don't understand at work
objectives: Ask someone to repeat or slow down politely
Ask what a word or instruction means
Ask for help or guidance at work
Use polite question forms: Could you...?, Would you mind...?, May I...?

phrases: I'm sorry, I didn't understand. Could you say that again?
Could you show me how to do this?
May I ask you a question?
Is this correct, or did I make a mistake?
target_language.grammar_pattern:
COULD YOU for polite requests
  Could you repeat that? (more polite than 'Repeat that')
  Could you show me how to do this?
  Could you speak more slowly, please?

WOULD YOU MIND + verb-ing
  Would you mind showing me again? (very polite)
  Would you mind if I asked you something?

MAY I for formal permission
  May I ask you a question?
  May I take a short break?

I'M SORRY / I DIDN'T UNDERSTAND — softeners
  I'm sorry, I didn't catch that.
  I'm not sure I understood. Could you explain?
  Excuse me — I didn't hear you clearly.

grammar_patterns.label: COULD YOU for polite requests
examples: Could you repeat that, please?
Could you speak a little more slowly?
Could you show me how to use this machine?
Could you write it down for me?

grammar_patterns.label: WOULD YOU MIND + verb-ing
examples: Would you mind showing me again?
Would you mind explaining that step?
Would you mind speaking more slowly?
Would you mind if I asked you something?

grammar_patterns.label: I didn't understand — clarification phrases
grammar_patterns.pattern: I'm sorry / I didn't + [catch / understand / hear] + Could you...?
examples: I'm sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you repeat it?
I didn't understand that word. What does it mean?
Excuse me, I didn't hear you clearly.
I'm not sure I understood. Could you explain?

story.context: It is Ahmed's first week at the warehouse. His supervisor, Lisa, is training him. Ahmed needs to ask for help and clarification several times.

dialogue.speaker: Lisa
dialogue.text: Good morning, Ahmed. Today I'll show you how to process incoming shipments. First, you scan the barcode on each box.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: I'm sorry — could you repeat that? I didn't hear the first part.

dialogue.speaker: Lisa
dialogue.text: Of course! You scan the barcode on each box with this scanner. Then you put the box on the correct shelf.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: Thank you. Could you show me how to use the scanner? I haven't used one before.

dialogue.speaker: Lisa
dialogue.text: Sure! Point it here, press this button, and wait for the beep. Easy, right?

dialogue.speaker: Lisa
dialogue.text: Go ahead. Now, after you scan everything, you fill out a receiving report.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: Excuse me — what does 'receiving report' mean?

dialogue.speaker: Lisa
dialogue.text: Good question. A receiving report is a form where you write what came in — how many boxes, what's inside, and any damage.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: I understand now. Would you mind showing me the form? I want to make sure I fill it in correctly.

dialogue.speaker: Lisa
dialogue.text: Absolutely. And Ahmed — please always ask if you're not sure. It's better to ask than to make a mistake.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: Thank you, Lisa. I will always ask. I want to do this job well.

drills.title: Could You...? Requests
drills.instruction: Make a polite request. Use: Could you + [verb] + please?

prompts.sentence: Could you ___ me how to do this?
Could you ___ that down for me?

examples: Could you repeat that, please?
Could you explain that step again?
Could you show me where the form is?
Could you speak a little more slowly?
Could you check my work when you have a moment?
drills.your_turn: Could you check my work when you have a moment?

drills.title: Would You Mind...?
drills.instruction: Make a very polite request. Use: Would you mind + [verb-ing]?
examples: Would you mind showing me how to do that?
Would you mind repeating the instructions?
Would you mind speaking more slowly?
Would you mind explaining this word?
Would you mind checking this for me?
drills.your_turn: Would you mind checking this for me?

drills.title: I Didn't Understand — Clarification
drills.instruction: Say that you didn't understand and ask for help. Use the clarification phrases.

prompts.sentence: I'm sorry, I ___ catch that. Could you repeat?
I ___ understand that word. What does it mean?
Excuse me, I didn't hear you ___.
I'm not ___ I understood. Could you explain?

examples: I'm sorry, I didn't catch that.
Could you repeat the last part?
I didn't understand that instruction.
What does that word mean?
Excuse me — could you say that again?
drills.your_turn: Excuse me — could you say that again?

listening.question: What does the worker ask the supervisor to do?
listening.transcript: I'm sorry, I didn't understand. Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
listening.explanation: The worker says 'Could you repeat that more slowly, please?' He didn't understand the instructions the first time and uses a polite request form to ask for help.

listening.question: How does the employee ask about a word she doesn't know?
listening.transcript: Excuse me, what does that word mean?
options: She looks it up on her phone
She ignores it and continues working
She asks 'What does that word mean?'
She asks her coworker to explain in her language
listening.explanation: The employee says 'Excuse me, what does that word mean?' This is the natural and correct way to ask about unfamiliar vocabulary at work.

listening.question: What does the supervisor say when the worker asks for help?
listening.transcript: Always ask if you're not sure. It's better to ask than to make a mistake.
options: She tells him to figure it out alone
She says 'Please always ask if you're not sure'
She tells him to read the manual
She gives him a written guide
listening.explanation: The supervisor says 'Always ask if you're not sure. It's better to ask than to make a mistake.' This is a common workplace attitude that encourages questions.

speaking.title: Ask for Clarification
speaking.instruction: Record yourself using 3 different clarification phrases in 3 short sentences. Imagine your supervisor just gave you instructions you didn't fully understand.
speaking.example: I'm sorry, I didn't catch the last part. Could you repeat that, please? Also, what does 'receiving report' mean? And would you mind showing me the correct form? Thank you for your patience.

speaking.title: Polite Requests at Work
speaking.instruction: Record yourself making 3 polite requests using: Could you...?, Would you mind...?, and May I...?
speaking.example: Could you show me where to put these boxes? Would you mind checking my work before I continue? And may I ask you one more question about the process? I want to make sure I do everything correctly.

writing.title: A Work Clarification Conversation
writing.instruction: Write a short conversation (5-6 lines) where a new worker asks for help or clarification on the job. Use at least 2 polite request forms (Could you...?, Would you mind...?, May I...?).
writing.example:
Supervisor: Put all the red boxes on shelf B and the blue boxes on shelf C.
Worker: I'm sorry, could you repeat that? I didn't hear which shelf.
Supervisor: Red boxes go on shelf B. Blue boxes on shelf C.
Worker: Thank you. Would you mind showing me where shelf B is? I'm still learning the layout.
Supervisor: Of course — follow me. And please always ask if you need help.

writing.title: Phrases I Need at Work
writing.instruction: Write 4 sentences using polite request language for situations you might face at work. Think about real things you might not understand: instructions, words, equipment, processes.
writing.example: Could you show me how to use the forklift safely? I don't know how to operate it yet. Would you mind explaining the safety rules before I start? I also want to know what 'inventory check' means — could you tell me? I want to do this job well and I will always ask when I am not sure.

sections.title: COULD YOU vs CAN YOU — both polite, different levels
examples: Can you help me? (informal, natural with coworkers)
Could you help me? (more polite — better with supervisors)
Can you repeat that? ✓ (fine between colleagues)
Could you repeat that, please? ✓ (more polite — better in formal situations)
Please repeat. ✗ (too direct — sounds like a command)
sections.question: When should I use COULD instead of CAN?
sections.explanation: CAN is fine for quick requests with coworkers you know well. COULD sounds more polite and respectful — use it with supervisors, customers, or in more formal situations. Adding 'please' to either makes it even more polite. The most important rule: avoid using the imperative ('Repeat.' / 'Show me.') — always soften with CAN, COULD, or WOULD YOU MIND.

sections.title: WOULD YOU MIND + verb-ing — a very polite structure
examples: Would you mind showing me? ✓
Would you mind to show me? ✗ (no 'to' after 'mind')
Would you mind repeat? ✗ (must add -ing)
Would you mind speaking more slowly? ✓
The answer 'No, not at all' = Yes, I will help you (confusing for learners!)
sections.question: What form does the verb take after WOULD YOU MIND?
sections.explanation: After WOULD YOU MIND, always use verb-ing (the gerund). Never use 'to + verb'. This structure is very polite and appropriate for any work situation. One important note: when someone answers 'No, not at all' — they mean 'I don't mind, I'm happy to help.' It sounds like 'no' but means 'yes, I will help.'

practice.sentence: Would you mind ___ me the form?

sections.title: Asking What Something Means
examples: What does 'receiving report' mean?
What does that word mean?
I don't understand. Could you explain?
Excuse me, what does this mean?
sections.question: How do we ask about a word or instruction we don't understand?
sections.explanation: Use 'What does [word] mean?' to ask about a specific word. You can also say 'I don't understand' or 'Could you explain?' for a whole instruction.

quiz.question: Which is the most polite way to ask your supervisor to repeat instructions?
quiz.explanation: 'Could you repeat that, please?' is polite, natural, and appropriate for the workplace. Bare imperatives like 'Repeat that' can sound rude.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses WOULD YOU MIND?
options: Would you mind to explain that?
Would you mind if explain that?
quiz.explanation: After WOULD YOU MIND, use verb + -ing. 'Would you mind explaining that?' is correct. Never use 'to + verb' after 'mind'.

quiz.question: Ahmed says 'I'm sorry, I didn't catch that.' What does 'catch' mean here?
options: He didn't understand or hear what was said
quiz.explanation: 'I didn't catch that' is an informal idiom meaning 'I didn't hear or understand.' It is very common in workplaces. 'I didn't catch the last part' = 'I didn't understand the end of what you said.'

quiz.question: How do you ask what a word means at work?
options: What is meaning of that word?
quiz.explanation: 'What does that word mean?' is the natural, correct form. The structure is: What does + [noun] + mean? You can also say 'What does [word] mean exactly?' or 'Could you explain what [word] means?'

quiz.question: Lisa says 'It's better to ask than to make a mistake.' What is she encouraging?
options: Ahmed to never do anything without permission
Ahmed to ask questions when he is not sure
Ahmed to read every instruction carefully
Ahmed to avoid making any decisions
quiz.explanation: Lisa is encouraging Ahmed to ask questions when he doesn't understand. This is important workplace advice — most supervisors prefer workers who ask rather than guess and get it wrong.

quiz.question: When your supervisor says 'Would you mind checking this?', what should you do?
options: Ask them why they need your help
Check the item they are referring to — it is a polite request for help
Ignore it — it was just a question
quiz.explanation: 'Would you mind...?' is a polite way to ask for help. When your supervisor uses it, they are asking you to do something. 'No, not at all' means 'I'm happy to help' — it is the polite way to accept.

quiz.question: Which phrase correctly asks for permission to try something?
quiz.explanation: 'May I try it?' is the natural, polite way to ask for permission. MAY I is slightly more formal than CAN I. Both are acceptable at work.

quiz.question: What is the difference between CAN YOU and COULD YOU?
options: CAN YOU is wrong at work
COULD YOU is only for managers
COULD YOU is more polite and respectful than CAN YOU
quiz.explanation: Both CAN YOU and COULD YOU work. COULD YOU sounds more polite and is better when speaking with supervisors or in formal situations. CAN YOU is fine with close coworkers.

quiz.question: Write 2 polite requests you might need to make on your first day at work. Use Could you...? or Would you mind...?
quiz.explanation: Think about your first day at a new job. What would you need help with? Practice the language now so it feels natural when you need it.

quiz.question: Your supervisor gives you a long list of instructions very quickly. You didn't understand everything. What do you say? Write 2-3 sentences.
quiz.explanation: Use your clarification phrases: I'm sorry, I didn't catch all of that. Could you repeat the last part? Or: Would you mind going through that again more slowly? It is professional to ask — not a sign of weakness.

somali.description: Baro sida caawimo loo waydiisto, tilmaanta dib loogu celiyo, loona caddaysto waxa aadan fahmin goobta shaqada
objectives: Si edeb leh u waydiiso qof inuu hadalka kuu celiyo ama gaabiyo
Waydiiso caawimo ama hagid goobta shaqada
Isticmaal qaababka su'aalaha edebta leh: Could you...?, Would you mind...?, May I...?

sections.explanation: CAN way ku fiican tahay codsiyada degdegga ah ee shaqo-wadaagta aad si fiican u taqaanno. COULD waxay u dhawaaqdaa si edeb iyo ixtiraam badan — la isticmaal kormeerayaasha, macaamiisha, ama xaaladaha rasmiga ah. 'please' ku darista waxay ka dhigaysaa mid ka sii edeb badan. Qaanuunka ugu muhiimsan: iska ilaali qaabka amarka ('Repeat.' / 'Show me.') — mar walba ku jilci CAN, COULD, ama WOULD YOU MIND.
examples: Can you help me? (aan rasmiga ahayn, dabiici ah asxaabta shaqada)
Could you help me? (ka ixtiyaar badan — waxaa ku habboon kormeerayaasha)
Can you repeat that? ✓ (waxay ku fiican tahay asxaabta shaqada dhexdooda)
Could you repeat that, please? ✓ (ka ixtiyaar badan — waxaa ku habboon xaaladaha rasmiga ah)
Please repeat. ✗ (aad bay u toosantahay — waxay u egtahay amar)

sections.explanation: WOULD YOU MIND ka dib, mar walba isticmaal fal-ing (gerund). Weligaa ha isticmaalin 'to + fal'. Qaabkani aad buu u edeb badan yahay, wuxuuna ku habboon yahay xaalad kasta oo shaqo ah. Hal qodob oo muhiim ah: marka qofku ku jawaabo 'No, not at all' — waxay ka dhigan tahay 'Dhib igama haysato, waan ku faraxsanahay inaan ku caawiyo.' Waxay u dhawaaqdaa 'maya' laakiin waxay ka dhigan tahay 'haa, waan ku caawin doonaa.'
examples: Would you mind showing me? ✓
Would you mind to show me? ✗ (ma jiro 'to' ka dib 'mind')
Would you mind repeat? ✗ (waa inaad ku darto -ing)
Would you mind speaking more slowly? ✓
Jawaabta 'No, not at all' waxay la macna tahay 'Yes, I will help you' (taas oo ardayda ku khaldami kartaa!)

sections.explanation: Isticmaal 'What does [word] mean?' si aad u weydiiso erey gaar ah. Waxa kale oo dhahdaa 'I don't understand' ama 'Could you explain?' tilmaan dhan.
examples: Waa maxay macnaha 'receiving report'?
Waa maxay macnaha ereygaas?
Ma fahmin. Ma i sharxi kartaa?
Cafis, waa maxay macnaha tan?

target_phrases: Fadlan, ma ku celin kartaa taas?
Fadlan, ma hadli kartaa si qunyar?
Waan ka xumahay, ma fahmin. Fadlan, mar kale dhihi kartaa?
Ma i tusi kartaa sida tan loo sameeyo?
Ma sax baa, mise qalad baan sameeyay?
dialogue: Subax wanaagsan, Ahmed. Maanta waxaan ku tusi doonaa sida loo qaado alaabta soo gasha. Marka hore, waxaad skaan gareeysaa barcode-ka sanduuq kasta.
Waan ka xumahay — ma mar kale dhihi kartaa? Qaybtii hore ma aan maqlin.
Dabcan! Waxaad skaan gareeysaa barcode-ka sanduuq kasta skaanerkan. Kadibna sanduuqa waxaad saartaa shelf-ka saxda ah.
Mahadsanid. Ma i tusi kartaa sida loo isticmaalo skaanerka? Weligay mid ma aan isticmaalin.
Haa! Halkan ku jeedi, badhankan riix, oo sug dhawaqa. Waa fududahay, miyaanay ahayn?
Haa! Ma aan isku dayi karaa?
Samee. Hadda, markaad wax walba skaan gareeyso, waxaad buuxinaysaa foomka alaabta soo gasha.
Su'aal wanaagsan. Waa foom lagu qoro waxa soo galay — inta sanduuq, waxa ku jira, iyo dhaawac kasta.
Hadda waan fahmay. Ma i tusi kartaa foomka? Waxaan rabaa inaan hubiyo inaan si sax ah u buuxiyo.
Hubaal. Ahmed, fadlan had iyo jeer waydii haddii aadan hubin. Inaad weydiiso ayaa ka fiican inaad qalad sameyso.
Mahadsanid, Lisa. Had iyo jeer waan waydiin doonaa. Waxaan doonayaa inaan shaqadan si fiican u qabto.
